parsed.label: punctuation after thought or code
parsed.trigger_hypothesis: The neuron activates strongly on punctuation marks (especially '&', ':', '.', '.ext') that appear after a thought, title, or code context, often when the preceding text is a complete phrase or a label.
parsed.output_hypothesis: The neuron's activation may signal the end of a thought or a label, preparing to transition to a new clause or detail.
alternatives: The neuron detects specific punctuation characters regardless of context.
The neuron responds to the end of a line or sentence in code or narrative.
parsed.adapter_changes: State E+1 generally increases activation in chat and emotional_chat domains, while state D+1 decreases it. State C+1 shows mixed effects with some large increases on specific tokens (e.g., 'play' in W21).

proposed_tests.discriminates: punctuation after a thought vs. punctuation within a word
colon after a title vs. colon in time
ampersand in code reference vs. ampersand in company name
period after a complete sentence vs. period in abbreviation
dot in file extension vs. dot in decimal number
punctuation after a thought in chat vs. punctuation in code comment
period after narrative thought vs. period in list
colon after label in response vs. colon in URL
ampersand in pointer syntax vs. ampersand in regular text
period after knock sound vs. period in middle of sentence
